titleStmt.title: Ovid, Amores 3.2: witness S — first-pass manuscript transcription
titleStmt.author: Publius Ovidius Naso

respStmt.resp: First-pass inspection of every extant verse image and manuscript encoding
respStmt.name: OpenAI Codex, encode_s agent

publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Awaiting independent second source reading; not human scholarly approval.

handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 386, 387, 388 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 84 extant verse positions were first-read directly from witness S images. Existing annotation rectangles are reproduced without modification. No reading is supplied from LL or another witness. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial. Independent second reading remains required.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. A missing written initial is represented as gap, without inventing its decoration. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.

interpretation.p: Notes are a first-reader evidence queue. Local uncertainty is documentation rather than an automatic user task. A different reader must independently inspect each verse and investigate all notes before integration.

div.head: First-pass encoding notes
div.note: The initial N is not inscribed before on; a one-character notInscribed gap records the source, not a reconstructed decorated initial. The middle word looks s·eo and the following word studios, without a secure full expansion. A small two-line right inscription begins ad amicā; its remainder is not safely recoverable. Inspect full page386 and margin1 crop.
The visible sequence is Cui m̄i ipse faues. The contracted m̄i is expanded mihi; ipse is preserved as written, without normalization to another gender.

The visible sequence begins Ne t̄ non notꝰ quē facis ē amor. The small t-like form and the notꝰ suspension are retained with tentative conventional expansions; no extra c or final m is supplied to the displayed source.

The final two words carry suspension marks, represented spectem̄ utr̄qꝫ and expanded spectemus uterque. Their exact distribution of minims and marks should be checked independently alongside the parallel abbreviation in6.

Two e-like marked forms occur after c̄tigit. The second is heavy and crossed-looking. Their function and possible relationship are not secure; both visible marked forms are retained without manufacturing an esse expansion, cancellation or replacement reading.
A stroke within currenti is distinctly darker. Dark ink alone does not identify a deleted earlier word or another historical hand.

The central marked sequence following suę is not securely resolved and is represented locally as unclear uic̄tī. Darker strokes are visible in fauore and puellę. No familiar verb form is silently substituted.
The line uses contracted dn̄ę and q̄sqꝫ, with conventional expansions dominę and quisque. Visible source e caudata is retained.
This verse begins actual manuscript387, despite viewer index388. Hec in lege loci is retained; circꝰ and h̄t are abbreviated. Page-edge fading does not justify missing words.
The contracted forms after Tu and after a are read t̄m and dext̄. The following contraction q̄cūqꝫ is expanded quicumque. Expansion does not add written letters to the source display.
The visible sequence is C̄tactu lat̄is ledē illam. The contractions are retained and expanded conservatively; no additional tui or passivizing verb ending is supplied from another witness.

A faint e-like trace stands between pudor and rigido. After the stop following genu a small right inscription looks t̄ manu; its function and first sign are unclear. It is encoded separately as manuscript marginal text.
The marked letter after Collige resembles ē. Its relation to the following clear en is uncertain; the literal marked form is retained without an asserted expansion or deletion.
The name after Talia appears metanion, but its internal strokes remain uncertain. The source spelling athalantis is retained; no standard form of either name is substituted.
The source reads ex istis with a word division; the et ligature and contractions cēt̄a and placē are separately represented.
Interea is darker and visually disturbed, but the current letters remain legible. No earlier erased reading is reconstructed.
The final stroke/mark of feminē is ambiguous. The visible marked form is retained without deciding an expanded ending solely from grammar.
Linguis is darker; pōpa and uen̄ are suspended forms. The source begins Si iam pompa, as encoded, and no familiar opening is imposed.
A rightward dea is clearly present separately from the baseline ending amor. It is retained as an addition without an unsupported replacement relationship.
The suspended word after pace is represented r̄ptus and expanded repertus. Its crowded contraction marks should be checked independently; no letters are silently inserted into the displayed form.
The source has a contracted pheobꝰ followed by written phebe. Both remain in the transcription. The sequence is not normalized to remove an apparent repeated name.
The contractions īte and ūt̄ are expanded in te and uertite. Their exact letter/mark allocation remains a palaeographical check, not a reason to fill from an edition.
Castora has darker strokes. The witness form is retained without emendation or inference of a historical hand.
The disturbed opening after Vota is not safely expanded and remains locally unclear as Vota dūm. The darker current sequence incoeptis is retained; no earlier state is invented.
The contracted form after nouę appears mēte and is provisionally expanded mente. The current strokes alone determine the source display; the expected syntax is not used to supply missing words.
A small hooked/caret-like sign occurs to the right of the verse. Its shape is represented schematically and declared; no insertion relationship is asserted.
The ending visibly appears rogam, without a securely visible final us sign. The source form remains unexpanded. Contractions in promisit and promittas are retained.
The crossed initial p is represented by a declared schematic per sign. The remainder includes t̄, pōpaqꝫ and a rum ending sign; conventional expansions remain separate from the source display.
The first verse on actual388 is faded toward its opening and right. Sed pendent t̄ crura potes si forte iuuabit is the visible reading; the first reader has not supplied extra words.

The marked word after uacuo is represented p̄ter without expansion because the visible contraction does not securely establish a particular full form. Page-top fading is retained as an evidence limitation.
The short marked sequence after Quadriiugos is locally unclear eq̄. No equus, equos or aequo expansion is imposed from expected syntax.
The ending of fauebis is a first-reader tentative reading and remains locally unclear. The contracted cuicūqꝫ is preserved.
The source contraction after admoto is represented p̄ximū and conventionally expanded proximum. A possible alternative ending must be decided from the marks, not normalized syntax.
The visible sequence Fauimꝰ ignauo is retained, including its suspended ending; the following s̄ and enī are contracted. Modern punctuation is not supplied.
A crossed per sign precedes date, which has a visible cancelling stroke. The deletion is recorded, while the following iactatis remains baseline text.
The source reads En reuocant at ne turbet. The words are preserved without replacement from a familiar edition.
The marked form ratā is retained with its bar; because the function of this mark is not established, no unmarked rata or final nasal is imposed as an expansion.
Initial S̄t̄ and final sup̄s̄t are heavily contracted and receive provisional conventional expansions Sunt and supersunt. All visible source marks remain in the transcription.
An initial Palma is crossed out before Ille; the deletion is visible and recorded. The later palmā is an ordinary contraction. The repeated noun is not removed silently.
The internal marked sequence qd̄dā is expanded quiddam provisionally; its exact pen-stroke grouping should be rechecked. The source has a dot after Risit and an et ligature.
